definitions.definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system.
definitions.example: A messy room has high entropy; a tidy room has low entropy.

definitions.definition: When parts of a system are in sync or aligned with each other.
definitions.example: A choir singing in perfect harmony is coherent; a crowd shouting random words is not.

definitions.definition: The process where a system loses its alignment and becomes random or disordered.
definitions.example: Ice cubes melting into a puddle of water is a form of decoherence.

definitions.definition: A symbol used in this framework to represent the coherence function, a measure of order or alignment.
definitions.example: Think of χ like a score from -1 (total chaos) to +1 (perfect order).

definitions.definition: A mathematical equation that describes how a system changes over time, especially in quantum physics.
definitions.example: It's like a recipe that tells you how a mixture will evolve from one state to another.

definitions.definition: A symbol used in this framework to represent the state of coherence or decoherence, ranging from +1 to -1.
definitions.example: σ = +1 means perfect order; σ = -1 means total chaos.

definitions.definition: Different ways of looking at or measuring the same thing, like using a ruler versus a scale.
definitions.example: Temperature can be measured in Celsius or Fahrenheit; those are different measurement frames.

definitions.definition: A judgment about what is good or bad, right or wrong, based on a standard.
definitions.example: Saying 'stealing is wrong' is a normative assessment.

definitions.definition: Signal-to-noise ratio, a measure of how clear a signal is compared to background noise, expressed in decibels.
definitions.example: A good radio station has high SNR; static has low SNR.

definitions.definition: When waves or cycles are synchronized so their peaks and troughs match up.
definitions.example: Two pendulums swinging in perfect sync have phase alignment.

definitions.definition: Heart rate variability, a measure of the time between heartbeats, often used as an indicator of health.
definitions.example: A healthy person usually has higher HRV than someone who is stressed or sick.

definitions.definition: Substances in the body that indicate how the immune system is functioning.
definitions.example: White blood cell count is an immune marker.

definitions.definition: When the parts of an organization or society work together smoothly and consistently.
definitions.example: A school where rules are clear and everyone follows them has institutional coherence.

definitions.definition: A term from this framework meaning alignment with the divine order or logic of the universe.
definitions.example: It's like being in tune with the 'big picture' purpose of everything.

definitions.definition: Being in a state of coherence with the fundamental field of order (the chi-field).
definitions.example: A well-tuned guitar string is aligned; a loose one is not.

definitions.definition: The ability of an object or system to hold together and not break apart.
definitions.example: A bridge with good structural integrity can support heavy loads.

definitions.definition: The flow of order or energy into a system to keep it organized and alive.
definitions.example: Eating food provides negentropy flux to your body.

definitions.definition: The number of independent ways a system can move or change.
definitions.example: A car has degrees of freedom: it can go forward, backward, and turn.

definitions.definition: The maximum amount of information that can be sent through a communication channel without error.
definitions.example: A fiber optic cable has a higher channel capacity than a tin can and string.

definitions.definition: When two or more waves have the same frequency and are in sync.
definitions.example: Two tuning forks that vibrate at the same pitch have frequency alignment.

definitions.definition: When different parts of the brain are firing in sync, often linked to focus or calmness.
definitions.example: Meditation can increase neural coherence.

definitions.definition: The idea that what is right or wrong depends on a person's culture, society, or personal feelings.
definitions.example: Someone who says 'stealing is okay in some cultures' is expressing moral relativism.

definitions.definition: A law of physics that says disorder (entropy) in a closed system always increases over time.
definitions.example: An ice cube melts in a warm room because the Second Law says disorder increases.

definitions.definition: The study of where words come from and how their meanings have changed.
definitions.example: Learning that 'holy' comes from a word meaning 'whole' is an example of etymology.

definitions.definition: The earliest form of the English language, spoken in England from about 450 to 1150 AD.
definitions.example: Beowulf was written in Old English.

definitions.definition: An Old English word meaning 'whole, complete, uninjured,' from which the modern word 'holy' comes.
definitions.example: It is pronounced 'HAH-lig'.

definitions.definition: A Latin phrase meaning 'its own end' or 'self-limiting,' used as a section title.
definitions.example: It is pronounced 'TER-mi-nus SOO-ee'.

definitions.definition: A concept in this framework referring to a reversal of values or order, possibly where good is called evil and vice versa.
definitions.example: It is like calling darkness 'light' and light 'darkness'.
